text:
maria: quick post — ran a small speculative-decoding pass on the new llama3-70b q4_0 model (internal qkit profile). goal: check latency win vs full decode and surface any obvious quality regressions before a canary.
jason: nice, what config did you try?
maria: baseline: greedy on q4_0 (no speculative). spec config that beat it: two-stage spec with draft=llama3-7b (float32) and verify on 70b-qat. params below.
maria: ```
spec.draft_model=redwood/llama3-7b-draft
spec.verify_model=redwood/llama3-70b-q4_0
spec.draft_beam=1
spec.draft_max_step=4
spec.confidence_thresh=0.82
spec.speculative_batch=16
runtime.kv_cache=true
```
oliver: results?
maria: microbench (1000 mixed-length prompts, seq=512 median):
- baseline latency p50=310ms, p95=980ms
- speculative p50=210ms, p95=740ms
- speedup ~1.45x p50, ~1.32x p95
maria: quality quick-check (eval harness on 200 NLI + 200 generation prompts):
- exact-match NLI: baseline 86.2%, spec 85.9% (delta -0.3pp)
- BLEU-like gen score: baseline 27.1, spec 26.8 (delta -0.3)
- safety regressions: none detected in sample set
perf-bot: auto-eval summary: latency_improvement=45%_p50, quality_delta=-0.35pp_overall, flagged=0
sophia: that's promising. what's the failure mode? where spec reverted too often?
maria: observed reverify rate ~12% overall, higher on long-coherent-dialog prompts (up to 25%). Most reverify hits came from draft hallucinating extra tokens that diverged semantically.
jason: what about temperature / sampling? did you run sampling tests (temp=0.8) vs greedy?
maria: yes — spec is more brittle under higher temp. at temp=0.8, reverify ~22% and quality delta increased to -1.1pp. so for now recommend spec only under deterministic decodes or low temp.
oliver: any quantization interactions? q4_0 vs q4_1?
maria: tried q4_1 on a smaller sweep — slightly higher quality (0.15pp) but latency ~5% worse. q4_1 + spec still wins vs baseline q4_0 greedy for p50 but margin shrinks.
jason: reproducibility: can you drop the exact run command? will add to perf dashboard.
maria: yep:
maria: ```bash
./run_spec_eval.sh \
  --draft redwood/llama3-7b-draft \
  --verify redwood/llama3-70b-q4_0 \
  --prompts datasets/minibench-mix.jsonl \
  --seed 42 \
  --temp 0.0 \
  --batch 32 \
  --out /tmp/spec-run-191250
```
perf-bot: artifact saved at https://internal.redwood/push/191250/spec-run-191250 (logs + eval csv)
oliver: what's the suggested rollout? canary % and gating metrics?
maria: suggested plan:
- canary 5% traffic on dedicated pool with spec enabled
- gating: end-to-end latency p95 <= baseline p95 * 0.95 (we want not worse), quality drop <= 0.5pp on main eval suite, no safety hits
- monitor reverify rate, prefix-cache hit rate, and top-10 divergence tokens
jason: add an emergency kill that disables spec if quality drift > 1pp for 30m
maria: done, will add to the route policy: `rollback_on_quality=true`, alert to #eng-oncall
sophia: any next experiments?
maria: plan: test draft_model size tuning (7b vs 13b), explore adaptive confidence_thresh per prompt length, and run a larger eval (10k prompts) including long-dialogue and instruction-following tasks.
oliver: can you add a short note about dataset bias? draft model trained on similar web data may match style and hide degenerate failures.
maria: yes — will include a prompt set targeted at style/format edgecases.
jason: thanks for the quick run. if someone wants to pick this up, ping me and I'll allocate GPU cycles.
sophia: :thumbsup:
